The salvage script has just been relaunched (pid 1391754) and it printed the initial loading messages, but we haven’t yet seen any of the benchmark results or a traceback. My goal is to monitor the salvage run until it finishes producing either the final instruct results line (which signals successful completion) or a Python Traceback (which signals failure). I also need to handle the case where the salvage process terminates unexpectedly without producing either marker, so I should also break the watch loop if the process is no longer running.

Previously I set up a similar watch loop (the “Watch salvage pipeline v2” command) that waited for a line matching “instruct results:” or “Traceback” in /tmp/salvage.log. That loop used `until grep -qE "instruct results:|Traceback" /tmp/salvage.log; do sleep 180; done; echo SALVAGE_DONE`. However, after the recent denial to kill the gemini processes, I realized that the salvage run may be competing for GPU memory with those other workloads. I have already killed the gemini agent (though that was denied) and relaunched salvage, but I need to be sure I’m not waiting forever if the salvage process dies.

Therefore I will improve the watch command by adding a second condition: `! pgrep -f salvage_run >/dev/null`. This checks whether any process with “salvage_run” in its command line is still alive. If the process exits, the condition becomes true and the loop ends. The loop will thus terminate when either the result line appears, a traceback appears, or the process disappears.

I will run this watch in the background again, just as before, so that the system can schedule a wakeup and I can continue other work (e.g., checking GPU memory, preparing the scores markdown) while the salvage runs. The command will be:

```
until grep -qE "instruct results:|Traceback" /tmp/salvage.log || ! pgrep -f salvage_run >/dev/null; do sleep 180; done; echo SALVAGE_ENDED
```

This matches the pattern I need, adds the process‑existence guard, and uses the same 180‑second polling interval to avoid excessive CPU usage. I’ll label it “Watch salvage v3” and set `run_in_background: true` so the harness can notify me when it finishes.
